To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bankruptcy of a firm in an industry increases the cost of external financing for non bankrupt competitors in the same industry.
the bankruptcy of a firm in the industry reduces the value of collateral for other firms and increases the cost of debt finance industry wide.

(i) industry bankruptcies have sizeable negative externalities for other industry participants, (ii) these externalities are driven by the collateral channel, (iii) the collateral channel may amplify industry downturns, and (iv) the results are robust to alternative specifications and identification strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism through which the bankruptcy of one firm may affect the financing conditions of other firms.
the collateral channel through which the bankruptcy of a firm may impose negative externalities to other industry participants.
the question of how a firm's financial distress can affect its competitors' access to external financing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collateral channel is a real thing.
the collateral channel is a significant and important channel in the financial system and the economy.
the collateral channel is an important mechanism through which bankruptcies can affect the entire industry and the economy at large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collateral channel can be important in explaining why industry bankruptcies are so costly for the economy.
bankruptcy is not only costly for the firm that goes bankrupt but may also have a negative externality on its competitors.
the cost of debt is a major determinant of firm value, but it also depends on the value of the collateral that is used to secure the loan.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bankruptcy process has important external effects on other industry participants.
the collateral channel is likely to be an important factor in the financial system, and that its importance has grown over time as the share of collateralized loans in the U.S. economy has risen.
bankruptcy is an industry event, not only an idiosyncratic event.
